## v2.4.6 "Abacus" — the core learns arithmetic, and what overflow actually means

Three indexed addressing modes with their page-cross penalty, `ADC` and `SBC` across six modes each, and the compare group. An abacus is a device for carrying, which is most of what this release is about: carry into a high byte, carry into an accumulator, and the signed-overflow flag that is *not* carry and is the one most often got wrong.

**The emulation core is untouched.** No behaviour change to `rustynes-{cpu,ppu,apu,mappers,core}`. AccuracyCoin remains **141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder)** and nestest 0-diff. The RTL lives in the sibling repository, pinned at **`RustyNES_MiSTer@26d0fd9`**.

---

### What matches

| ROM | records | covers |
|---|---|---|
| `opgroup1` | **147/147** | v2.4.4's reset and implied group, unchanged |
| `opgroup2` | **140/140** | v2.4.5's addressing modes, loads, stores, branches, unchanged |
| `opgroup3` | **286/286** | every construct new in this release |

**573 records**, compared on `cycle`, `pc`, `a`, `x`, `y`, `p`, `s`. The two older ROMs are re-run every time precisely because a datapath this size is easy to improve in one place and break in another.

### Zero-page indexing wraps inside page zero

The add is 8-bit. `$FE + $05` is `$0003`, not `$0103`.

An implementation that indexes with a 16-bit add is wrong **only** for programs that index past `$FF` — which is exactly the kind of defect that survives casual testing, because almost nothing does it and the one thing that does is usually a table walk nobody notices. So the ROM does it deliberately, and reads the result back through a *different* addressing mode: a same-mode read-back round-trips through any wrong address and proves nothing, which v2.4.5 established the hard way.

### Absolute indexing pays for its page cross, and a write pays always

A read whose low-byte add did not carry takes **four** cycles. One that carried takes **five**: the CPU drove an address with an unfixed high byte, discovered the carry, and has to go again.

A **write takes five regardless.** The CPU has already driven the unfixed address, and it must not write there — so the fast path is unavailable to a store even when no page was crossed.

That distinction is invisible to a register comparison. An implementation that lets a store take the read fast path agrees on `a`, `x`, `y`, `p`, `s` and `pc` at every instruction boundary and differs only on `cycle`. It is in the trace for that reason.

### `ADC` and `SBC` share one adder

`SBC` feeds it `~M`. That is why the 6502 has no separate subtractor, and why `SBC`'s carry means **no borrow** — a distinction that reads like a convention until you write the adder and see that it is the same wire.

Overflow is **signed** overflow, not carry: set when the two operands share a sign and the result does not, which `(~(a ^ m) & (a ^ r))[7]` says exactly and says nothing else.

The ROM covers three cases because one cannot separate the two ways to get this wrong:

| case | carry | overflow |
|---|---|---|
| `$7F + $01 = $80` | no | **yes** |
| `$80 + $FF = $7F` | **yes** | **yes** |
| `$10 + $10 = $20` | no | no |

An implementation that computes V from the carry passes the second and fails the first. One with V stuck high passes the first two and fails the third. Three cases distinguish both from correct.

### A compare is a subtract whose result is discarded

The register is not written, and **V is not touched** — a compare has no signed-overflow meaning, and setting it there is a common quiet error. The ROM stores `A` after the compare sequence and reads it back, because "the register survived" is a claim that needs evidence rather than assertion.

---

### Mutations

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| baseline / restored | MATCH |
| indexed **write** takes the read fast path | **DIVERGE** |
| zero-page index does not wrap in page zero | **DIVERGE** |
| V computed from carry, not signed overflow | **DIVERGE** |
| `SBC` does not invert its operand | **DIVERGE** |
| `ADC` ignores carry-in | **DIVERGE** |
| compare sets carry inverted | **DIVERGE** |
| `zp,X` omits the un-indexed dummy read | **DIVERGE** |

### Designing for distinguishability is now the default

Every case in the new ROM is built so the **wrong answer differs from the right one**. That is not tidiness, it is a correction applied twice already: v2.4.4 shipped a `TXS` test whose wrong answer computed exactly the flags `TSX` had already left, and v2.4.5 shipped store/load pairs in the same addressing mode that round-trip through *any* wrong address. Both came back NOT CAUGHT under mutation, and neither was visible by reading the test.

### An instruction-set asymmetry, recorded because it reads like a typo

`LDX` and `STX` index by **Y**; `LDY` and `STY` index by **X**. An index register cannot index itself, so there is no `LDX zp,X`. The decode says so at the site, because the next person to read it will assume a copy-paste error.

### Provenance

Written from public documentation only — the NESdev wiki's 6502 cycle-times, instruction and addressing-mode pages, and this repository's own `docs/cpu-6502.md`. No reference NES core was opened; none is present in either tree, and CI asserts their absence.

### Next

v2.4.7: the stack group (`PHA`/`PLA`/`PHP`/`PLP`, `JSR`/`RTS`), `JMP` including the indirect page-boundary bug, and the read-modify-write group with its double write.

### Compatibility

Documentation and programme-record only on the RustyNES side. No save-state, movie, netplay or public-API change in any shipped or default-build package; `.rns` and `.rnm` are unchanged, and `rustynes-cosim` remains excluded from the workspace and the default build.
